notes: Reviewed unchanged: the accepted alignment is correct as it stands. All 14 source and 14 target ids are partitioned exactly once; every unit is aligned, with no unrepresented or added units in this verse, and every head is the sole token of a one-token unit under rule 10.

The verse is compositionally transparent and fully atomized: no source pair licenses a merge under rules 35, 39, 45 or 94, since the ASV writes a separate English word for every source token and no two tokens collapse into one.

s009 takes a bare *the* rather than *from the*. Rule 21 hands a case preposition to the article only where the Greek expresses no preposition; here apo is expressed and rule 36 keeps *from* on it, so the article anchors only the determiner and the noun stands bare.

s004 and s013 are the same lemma rendered two ways (*any*, *one*). Each is aligned to its own English word rather than merged into a shared unit; they are separate clause participants (the one who errs, and the one who converts him), so rule 24's same-analysis habit is satisfied by treating both as plain indefinites and not by giving them one unit.

Rule 36 is the only place this verse could plausibly have gone wrong: *err from* invites reading *from* as the verb's particle. The rule forbids it in terms, so *from* stays with apo and s007 keeps a bare *err*.
